title: Technology Sector Update for 09/10/2018: INTC,SAIC,ENG,I,SNAP - Nasdaq.com

Technology stocks were firming shortly before Monday's closing bell, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were adding more than 0.3% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was rising just under 1.0%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) Intel ( INTC ) was lower in late Monday trading, sliding back to negative ground following a see-saw session, following reports the chipmaker giant has acquired system-on-chip design firm NetSpeed Systems for an undisclosed amount. NetSpeed, which recently was valued at around $60 million, will become part of Intel's silicon engineering division, with CEO and former Intel employee Sundari Mitra rejoining the company.
In other sector news:
(+) Intelsat ( I ) rose as much as 3% on Monday after the satellite services company began a $1.69 billion cash tender offer for any or all of its 7.25% senior notes due 2020, paying an extra $36.25 in interest for each $1,000 of principal amount of the notes acrued prior to the Oct. 15 settlement date. The offer is scheduled to expire at 5 p.m. ET Friday, Sept. 14, unless extended or terminated early.
(-) Snap ( SNAP ) dropped over 2% on Monday, falling to within 4 cents of its 52-week low of $9.62 a share after saying in a regulatory filing that chief strategy officer Imran Khan is leaving the company to pursue other opportunities. Khan is expected to remain in his current role on an interim basis to assist with the transition of his responsibilities to coworkers. His last day on the job has not yet been determined, the company said.
(-) Science Applications International Corp ( SAIC ) tumbled Monday, sinking almost 12% in recent trading, after announcing its $2.5 billion, all-stock buyout of Englilty Holdings ( EGL ), swapping 0.45 of a share of its common stock for each Engility share. The acquisition upstaged better-than-expected Q2 financial results, with the technology integrator earning $1.13 per share during the three months ended July 31 on $1.12 billion in revenue. Analysts, on aveage, had been expecting the company to earn $0.99 per share on $1.11 billion in revenue.
